newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOJ wary of risking Japan recovery via rate hike.
newsitem.headline: BOJ wary of risking Japan recovery via rate hike.

text.p: Bank of Japan (BOJ) officials hinted on Tuesday that the central bank is content with maintaining its easy credit rather than putting the nation's embryonic economic recovery at risk by a premature tightening.
Japan's market interest rates have risen in the past few days on speculation that the BOJ may pronounce an end to its credit easing, which began in July 1991, by the middle of the year.
But policymakers on Tuesday indicated that it was not ready to venture a policy move, at least for now.
A senior BOJ official told Reuters that the risk of inflation in Japan is small compared with that of the nation's economy getting off a firm, self-sustainable recovery path.
"If we weigh inflationary risks and the risk of a fiscal drag undermining the potential for a self-sustainable economic recovery, the latter would be greater," he said.
The official said that although the potential was high for Japan to achieve a self-sustainable recovery, it was not assured.
The central bank reflects this observation in its current monetary policy, he added.

Some private economists estimate that a higher sales tax burden beginning in April, together with the abolition of a special income tax cut and an increase in social security payments, will drag down the economy by more than one percentage point this year.
The continuation of the recovery will depend on whether private sector demand will accelerate enough to overcome these fiscal drags, another government official said.

"The next policy move would be in late May at the earliest, but even then the central bank is unlikely to raise the official discount rate (ODR), but may just nudge up the key call rate, possibly by 25 basis points," said Shoji Kitta, president of Totan Research Co Ltd.
The BOJ could hold over the rate hike until early July when the outcome of its quarterly "Tankan" corporate survey in June will be available.

Economists said that the next "Tankan" survey due on April 2 is unlikely push the BOJ towards an early tightening, even though the survey is expected to confirm an improvement in business sentiment in the manufacturing sector.
The long wait and the reluctance to move the ODR reflect the central bank's fear that a premature, drastic policy change, might kill an economic recovery, Kitta said.
The BOJ's earlier decision to announce any changes in the key call rate target to the market will also make it extremely cautious in making a policy move, the second official said.
"Even the smallest rise in the call rate could be taken as an announcement and prompt an overshooting of interest rates across the yield curve," he said.
Since September 1995, the BOJ has been managing market liquidity to let the key call rate move below the 0.5 percent discount rate on average.
Meanwhile, economic research reports have upwardly revised Japan's growth forecast due mainly to the strong export growth prompted by the yen's steep fall over the past year.
Tokio Marine recently revised its economic growth forecast for fiscal 1997/98, starting April, to 1.8 percent from the previous 1.3 percent.

"The revision reflected strong export growth, rises in shipment of cars, computers and machine tools and the firm recoveries in consumption and capital investment," said Yoshiichi Taguchi, strategist at Tokio Marine MC Asset Management Co Ltd.
However, the first BOJ official said economic indicators gauging the health of the service sector, which has a bigger role than goods in Japan's overall economy, are not yet strong.
In contrast, indicators for manufactured goods have been strong, but that could change due to such variables as foreign exchange rates.
